target_customer: Direct to consumer brands buying YouTube creator sponsorships, and independent creators seeking brand deals
problem: D2C companies want an efficient alternative to Google and Facebook ads, and creators need help finding and negotiating sponsorships.
business_model: Two sided marketplace and agency taking a share of creator sponsorship billings

founders.name: Andres Felipe Diaz
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only a values oriented bio.

founders.name: Carlos Saavedra
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only a bio about empowering creators in 60+ countries.

competitors.name: FameBit
competitors.what: Self serve marketplace connecting brands with YouTube creators for sponsored videos
competitors.traction_then: About 9,000 YouTubers signed up by April 2015 and over 15,000 creators by August 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace and workflow layer for sponsorship deals with no deep technology; the work is sales and relationship management.

defensibility.rationale: Creator and brand relationships build slowly, but FameBit and agencies offered the same service and switching was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google acquired FameBit in 2016 and later folded it into YouTube BrandConnect, per a Wikipedia based summary. Makrwatch kept operating independently.

market_need_then: YouTube creator sponsorship spend was growing in 2015, evidenced by FameBit reaching 15,000 creators and acquiring Refame in 2015.

branding.domain_note: Uses makrwatch.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and reassuring; short headlines like 'Create more. Negotiate less.' and creator protection language.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand was found; the site claims 7,400+ creators sponsored over ten years but no outside source confirms brand recognition.

outcome_analysis: Makrwatch is still active with about 19 staff and fully remote, and the company reports growth and more than 27M distributed to creators on its own site. No outside source covers funding or an exit, so the record shows a small durable agency style business rather than a venture outcome. The story cannot be tied to taxonomy factors without independent sources.
notes: YC page gives founded 2017 while the batch is Winter 2015, an unexplained conflict. A directory shows an undisclosed seed in 2015 and CB Insights lists a 'MidGame' with 120K, both unverified and possibly a different entity (YC links the Crunchbase slug themidgame). Competitor FameBit source is dated August 2015, about five months after the batch. Search for outcome news returned nothing relevant. Site claims are self reported.
